site.sight:arena1: Six living oaks stand round a floor of mossy stone. A stone sits on a dais in the middle.
site.sight:arena2: Loose sand fills a bowl inside a gilded rim, with a stone on a gilded dais.
site.sight:arena3: Eight pillars of stacked bone, capped with azure crystal, ring a pad of dressed stone.
site.sight:arena4: Under a dome of fungus, four lamps hang over a stone.
site.sight:arena5: Tall masts stand round a stone. They are brick at the foot and glassed stone higher up.
site.sight:arena6: A disc of rock lies in open air, ringed in crystal. Single stones run off it and stop.
site.sight:arena7: Ten pillars of black glass stand round a stone in the open. Violet crystal caps them.
site.sight:arena8: Lanterns on eight stepped heaps ring a raised base of dressed stone with a stone on top.
site.sight:burned_hearths: The floor round the hearthstone is burned black. The rest of the house is whole.
site.sight:cache1: Square walls of dressed stone stand in the cavern, open at one narrow doorway.
site.sight:cache2: A small disc of turf hangs in open air with a chest on it. Nothing leads to it.
site.sight:column: From the summit a column of rubble one piece wide goes straight up and stops in the air.
site.sight:crossing: Single dressed stones stand in the water in a line out from the shore.
site.sight:dungeon: Rooms of dressed stone lie under the rock, joined by passages. Nothing leads up.
site.sight:fire_ring: Low sandstone houses ring a fire on a floor of black glass. Their doors face the fire.
site.sight:fold: Two short walls of rubble meet in a corner, with an oak standing in the angle.
site.sight:hearth: Set into the floor opposite the door is a block of dressed stone.
site.sight:lamp_row: Three fungus lamps hang in a straight line under the roof, evenly spaced.
site.sight:lone_tree: A pale tree with lit leaves stands by itself among white and blue flowers.
site.sight:pan: In the shore sandstone a square is cut one piece deep, inside a raised rim.
site.sight:prints: Prints run across the snow in a short line. Clean snow lies at both ends.
site.sight:quarry: A square bite is cut out of the slope, with flat faces. One half-dressed block is left.
site.sight:ruin: Stone walls with clean gaps stand round a paved floor. A lamp sits on a pillar.
site.sight:shaft: Walled in dressed stone, a square shaft goes straight down out of sight.
site.sight:stump: Among the standing spires are stumps of crystal one piece high.
site.sight:tree_floor: High among the trunks is a floor of planks with a lamp on it. Nothing leads up to it.
site.sight:village: Houses stand in a ring round a lit well, every door facing it.
codex.seen:place:0: The ground is sound in every direction, as far as any of us has walked. There is a sun, a moon, and stars that turn. Old stonework stands in every country, and most of it is empty.
codex.read:place:0: Our own grounds are thinning, and this one is sound wherever we go. A block left in the air stays there. At home only ground over dead wood holds that steady. We guess there is dead wood under all of this.
codex.born:place:0: This is the ground, peopl, and there is no other. The forebears raised the stones on it and built to the ends of it. It has always been sound.
codex.seen:place:1: There is no sky. Caverns open into caverns, lit by fungus and crystal, with rock and standing water between. Feeders are up here at every hour.
codex.read:place:1: Dug down, the floor of the hollow is the same black face we struck under the living ground, and no pick of ours marks it. If the roof is the same, the hollow lies between two faces of that stuff.
codex.born:place:1: Under is where the things of the night come from, and nobody holds a hearth down there. I will not go through your gate, peopl, and no householder will.
codex.seen:place:2: The ground here is islands in two layers, with open air between them and nothing below. The sun is just down and the stars stand still. Pale sheets hang under the lower layer.
codex.read:place:2: A step off an island does not land. The one who stepped is back on the last footing, hurt. The hour has not moved since we came. We take the islands to be overhead, as the hollow is under.
codex.seen:country:ocean: All the water lies at one height, over sand, with clay in the shallows and gravel further out. Fish swim in it. No feeder has been met in it at any hour.
codex.read:country:ocean: Lines of single dressed stones run out from the shore, and a few reach the far side. People crossed here on foot, a stone at a time, over water with nothing set in it for a feeder to take a body from.
codex.seen:country:beach: Sand lies over sandstone at the water, with reeds where the grass begins. No creature lives on the open shore. By day nothing is in the water on one side, with no cover on the other.
codex.read:country:beach: The sandstone under the shore is sand that has set again, as loose ground here does if it lies long enough. Pans for salt are cut into it.
codex.seen:country:plains: Grass runs open here, with a lone oak now and then. Sheep graze it in small flocks, with grouse in the long grass and Kinva sitting in it by day.
codex.read:country:plains: The corners of stone folds stand in this grass, each with an oak in the angle, and flocks were shut in here at night once. They still graze it, gone wild. Their grazing keeps the trees out.
codex.seen:country:palewood: Pale-barked trees make a light wood, with grass, flowers and berry bushes under them and a few young oaks coming up between. Sheep and grouse. Kantak stand among the bushes by day.
codex.read:country:palewood: Under these trees stands a village, and the flowers of open pasture still grow on the floor. The pale trees came in after the flocks thinned. Oak is coming up under them.
codex.seen:country:forest: Old oaks stand close here over fern, brown mushroom and berry bushes, with a pale tree here and there. Apples fall from the oaks. Sheep, grouse and boar live in it. Kantak and Kinva are out by day.
codex.read:country:forest: Where a village stands under the oaks, that ground was cleared and lived on, and the wood came back over it. Elsewhere the trees do not show whether it was ever cleared.
codex.seen:country:bloomvale: Short pale turf is thick with flowers, white and blue more than red, and the trees are in blossom. The turf is paler and bluer than the grass of the country round it.
codex.read:country:bloomvale: We have seen this turf and these white and blue flowers on the islands. Seed most likely came back through gates on feet and loads and took here.
codex.seen:country:swamp: Mud lies at the height of the sea under broad low oaks, reeds and mushrooms, in a haze that does not lift. Kaddam lie sunk in it with the head showing until a body comes near.
codex.read:country:swamp: Out of a Kaddam came a Lees Lump: lees set hard, as lees sets in rock, swallowed with the mud. Feeders that die in the mire sink where nobody boils them down.
codex.seen:country:taiga: Pine wood covers this cold country, with fern and more berry bushes than anywhere else. Snow lies on the higher ground. Boar root here by day. At night Vaka hunt it, one to three together.
codex.read:country:taiga: Nothing hostile is out here by day: the kinds that sit out the day in green country are bodied in growth, and pine wood has little of it. The villages are pine, stocked like the rest.
codex.seen:country:tundra: Snow lies flat over grass, with a pine or a dry bramble here and there and ice along the sea. Nobody built a village. By day nothing hostile walks it. A stone or a store shows from a long way off.
codex.read:country:tundra: There is no timber, fuel or flock here, and nobody raised a house. On this snow we saw prints begin in the middle of clean ground with no trail behind them.
codex.seen:country:desert: Sand lies deep over sandstone, with cactus and dry bramble on it, and villages of sandstone stand round wells. Hares run here by day. At night Angār come up over the sand.
codex.read:country:desert: The sand-country people live round fires on floors of black glass. Sand runs to glass only under a hard fire kept up a long time. The sand grows almost nothing that burns. Their fuel is carried in.
codex.seen:country:savanna: Tall dry grass grows between low flat-topped kapok trees standing far apart. Sheep and hares graze it. Kinva are out by day, Angār over the grass at night. Villages stand in it.
codex.read:country:savanna: In the wet wood the kapok grows close. Here it stands far apart, and this is the nearest timber to the sand. In some of these villages every hearth floor is burned black.
codex.seen:country:jungle: These are the tallest trees on the ground, in hot wet wood over fern. Grouse are the only animal in it. Kantak stand in the undergrowth. There is no village anywhere in it.
codex.read:country:jungle: No flock lives here to feed a hearth, so nobody built a village. The people who worked the stones of this country slept on plank floors high in the trunks.
codex.seen:country:crags: High stone, with grass on the flats, bare rock on the slopes and a few pines. Coal and iron show in the cliff faces without digging. At night Jatu hang under the overhangs.
codex.read:country:crags: Hard rock lies at the surface, and square bites are cut in the slopes with a half-dressed block at the foot of each. Hard stone for housings was cut here. Nobody came back for the blocks.
codex.seen:country:peaks: Nothing grows above the snow line. Snow lies over stone, coal shows in the faces, and Vaka and Jatu are out on it at night.
codex.read:country:peaks: Nobody could live up here. The only work of people is the columns of rubble on some summits, put up by someone with a way.
codex.seen:country:hollows: Fungal turf floors these caverns, set with glowing fronds and mushrooms. Where the roof is high, fungus stems stand as tall as trees. Antar ore runs through the rock.
codex.read:country:hollows: Fungus covers whatever dies down here, since nothing in the hollow is boiled down or burned. A row of lamp fungus hangs dead straight under one roof. That was a person's work.
codex.seen:country:hollows_crystal: Spires of azure and violet crystal stand on bare hollow rock, some taller than a person, and there is almost no fungus. The crystal lights the floor round it. Tala ore lies in the lower rock.
codex.read:country:hollows_crystal: Standing crystal is lees that nothing ate, and its colour follows the kind it came from. A great many of some violet kind died here and lay uneaten. None of that kind is here now.
codex.seen:country:rift: Turf over soil over island rock. Trees with lit leaves grow here among grass and white and blue flowers. Pale sheets hang under the edges. Vihanga and Kajjot fly overhead.
codex.read:country:rift: Island Fruit picked here neither ripens nor rots, and the sky has not moved since we first crossed. Everything here stands at one dusk.
codex.seen:country:rift_shards: Spires of pale crystal stand on these islands, with white flowers between and no trees. Sakal stand among the spires and do not move until something comes near.
codex.read:country:rift_shards: Some spires are eaten down to stumps one piece high. The Sakal we opened carried bits of the same crystal.
codex.seen:site:village: A few houses stand round a well, every door facing it, with one lamp over the well. Each house has a crate, a lamp, and a bedroll or a workbench. The crates are stocked, and nobody lives here.
codex.read:site:village: The one lamp at the well lights the ground between all the doors. A bedroll from one of these houses works for us as our own do. Somebody who slept in this village had a way.
codex.born:site:village: The forebears built these and lived in them, and a hearth went dark when nobody was left to sit at it. We pass nights in them on the road and leave the crates full.
codex.seen:site:ruin: Walls up to four pieces high stand round a paved floor, with clean gaps broken in them. A lamp stands on a pillar beside a chest. None of the stone is dressed. Under some floors is a nest.
codex.read:site:ruin: The chest still held gear and some lees, left there by whoever broke the walls. Nothing here is cut down into the rock, as the sealed stores are.
codex.born:site:ruin: Feeders broke into those, and the sand-country people on their marches. The forebears stored on top of the ground when they could no longer go under it, so look in the chest, peopl.
codex.sand:site:ruin: We broke some of those and burned what was in them. What is stored draws.
codex.seen:site:dungeon: Rooms of dressed stone lie deep under solid rock, joined by passages, with no way in from above and lamps or azure crystal on pillars. Most rooms hold a nest. The chest is in the last.
codex.read:site:dungeon: One chest held gear, lees, a bait made ahead and a recall stone. That stone works for any of us and for no born person. This store was stocked for hunters at the great stones who had a way.
codex.born:site:dungeon: Any of us who digs down to a sealed store does not come up. Bring a tool out of one whole, peopl. I want to see how the forebears worked.
codex.sand:site:dungeon: The stores under the rock are full because nobody went back for them. Empty the ones in the sand country before a march reaches them. Our people die breaking those.
codex.seen:site:cache1: One room of dressed stone stands in the cavern, seven strides square, with a doorway one piece wide. Inside are two fungus lamps, a chest, and a nest of Asikavak.
codex.read:site:cache1: Its chest held a Guhamāt Smoker, made and never laid. The stone is dressed like the stone of the sealed stores. The people who stocked those came into the hollow as well, through gates of their own.
codex.seen:site:cache2: Between the two layers hangs a disc of turf and island rock, with a chest and two posts of island timber capped with crystal. Nothing that walks reaches it.
codex.read:site:cache2: An island has no depth of rock to seal a room under, and this store is sealed by air instead. Its chest held a bait ready, as the vaults of the hollow do.
codex.seen:site:arena1: Six living oaks are the posts of a paved round of mossy stone, with glowing mushrooms in a ring. The stone sits on a dais of mossy brick.
codex.read:site:arena1: When the Vanahar came up, its roots went down into the joints of the paving and up the six oaks. It tore them out again halfway through. Root and moss hold this paving together.
codex.born:site:arena1: That is the Vanahar Altar. The forebears set the Vanahar over the woods when they raised it. One stands a short walk from where peopls come up.
codex.sand:site:arena1: Every stone feeds what lies at it. That one lies nearest the place peopls come up out of the ground.
codex.seen:site:arena2: The bowl is sunk three deep and filled with loose sand. Gilded brick rims it, four pillars stand on the rim, and the stone sits on a gilded dais in the sand.
codex.read:site:arena2: The Maruhar came up through the loose sand in the bowl. Bowls like this stand in green country too. The sand in them was carried there. Rim and dais are faced with gold, and its kind gets nothing from gold.
codex.born:site:arena2: Stand on the rim of the Maruhar Altar, peopl. The sand in the bowl is where it comes up.
codex.sand:site:arena2: Our burrower lay at these. It was the price of the sand, and it let nothing else in. Leave that stone bare and another will come onto the empty sand.
codex.seen:site:arena3: Eight pillars of stacked bone, each capped with azure crystal, stand on a pad of dressed stone and stone brick. At the foot of every second pillar a cell of the paving is crystal.
codex.read:site:arena3: The pillars are bone of the kind left in the pot after a boil, stacked. The azure caps are lees spilled from the pots and set. Animals of the Kankāl's kind were boiled on this floor, a great many of them.
codex.seen:site:arena4: A dome is cut in hollow rock, floored with fungal turf and lined with fungus cap. Six fungus stems with wide caps stand round the stone under four hanging fungus lamps.
codex.read:site:arena4: When the smoke reached the roof, the roof moved. The dome is the Guhamāt's own growth, and it hangs by it. Nobody can hold a stone where no dawn comes, so this one could only be baited.
codex.seen:site:arena5: Six tall masts stand round the stone on a pad of stone brick. Each is brick at the foot and turns to glassed stone toward the top.
codex.read:site:arena5: Its throws turned the brick soft where they struck, and it set again as glassed stone, on the pad and up the masts. The Jīmūt never landed. The masts are tall enough to fly a kite from.
codex.seen:site:arena6: Island rock five thick, flecked with crystal, laid as a disc in open air, with eight crystal pillars. A line of single stones runs out from the rim and stops.
codex.read:site:arena6: Set ground stays where it is laid, and somebody laid this floor in open air, with the way out to it one stone at a time. The flecks and pillars are lees, spilled from boiling and set.
codex.seen:site:arena7: Black glass and deep rock pave this floor under the open sky. Ten pillars of black glass stand on it, capped with violet crystal.
codex.read:site:arena7: Black glass and deep rock do not lie at the surface, and these were carried up. The Kuranga came only after dark. Its tines gave the violet light of the caps. Its kind was boiled down on this floor before us.
codex.born:site:arena7: The Kuranga Altar. Wear the mask at it after dark, peopl, and it comes up. It has never come under the sun.
codex.seen:site:arena8: Eight stepped heaps, each with a lantern, ring a raised base of dressed stone in three tiers. The stone sits on top.
codex.read:site:arena8: The Nihān came up through the base, and the base now stands hollow, eaten out from beneath. It looks to have been a store under the stone that the Nihān ate into from below.
codex.born:site:arena8: The Cairn. When the great lees ran out, the forebears closed their first and best stone under it, to save it for the day it can be lit again.
codex.sand:site:arena8: They closed that heap over a thing nobody could kill and set lamps round it. The stones fattened it like the others.
codex.seen:site:burned_hearths: In some houses here the floor round every hearthstone is burned black. The crates are stocked like any others. Nothing in the houses shows who did it.
codex.born:site:burned_hearths: Sand-country people did that on a march. They burn whatever they cannot carry home.
codex.sand:site:burned_hearths: The people of those houses burned their own floors on the day they walked out.
codex.seen:site:fire_ring: One fire burns day and night on a round floor of black glass. Low sandstone houses ring it with their doors to the fire. Fuel is stacked inside the ring. There is no chest, pot or bed.
codex.read:site:fire_ring: Broken out, the floor is grey glass with ash through it, the same stuff as the fighters' tokens. That much glass took one fire burning on the sand for a very long time.
codex.born:site:fire_ring: Their fires want more wood than the sand will ever grow, and I carry nothing to them.
codex.sand:site:fire_ring: Inside the light is the only safe ground we have now. Whoever has the fuel says who sleeps there.
codex.seen:site:hearth: Set into the floor of every old house, against the wall opposite the door, is a slab of dressed stone. It is the stone a householder sits at.
codex.read:site:hearth: Beneath one hearthstone in several lies a ward core, though householders hold at these same stones with nothing under them. Whoever set the cores built hearths as they are built at home.
codex.born:site:hearth: A hearthstone carries what the hand drives down into the pot. The forebears set one in every house. I cut the slabs householders carry on the road.
codex.seen:site:column: A column of rubble one piece wide stands far above a summit and ends in nothing. A bedroll lies at its foot, and a torch on the other side.
codex.read:site:column: The bedroll at its foot works for us. One of us stacked this, trying to build up to the islands, and stopped. No born person thinks anything is overhead.
codex.seen:site:crossing: Single dressed stones set at the waterline, open water between each, in a line out from the shore. A second stone stands on top of the last stone in the line.
codex.read:site:crossing: Someone walked out over the sea a stone at a time. A stone set at the waterline stays with nothing under it, and nothing comes up in water. The work stopped at the stone carried out and never set.
codex.seen:site:fold: Two runs of rubble two high meet at a right angle, with an oak standing in the angle.
codex.read:site:fold: No rubble lies where the rest of the wall would run, and nothing falls down here. Somebody carried it off. This was the corner of a fold, by the look of it, with one oak left for shade.
codex.seen:site:lamp_row: Three fungus lamps hang in a straight row under the roof, evenly spaced.
codex.read:site:lamp_row: Lamp fungus grows where its spores land, in no order. These three were hung. We followed two rows like this. Each led toward a vault or a stone.
codex.seen:site:lone_tree: Alone among the flowers stands a tree with a pale trunk and leaves that give light. Nothing comes up under it. Now and then its leaves drop a fruit.
codex.read:site:lone_tree: Its fruit is Island Fruit, and the flowers round it grow on the islands. A seed came back with somebody who crossed and took root.
codex.seen:site:pan: A square pan is cut one piece deep in the shore sandstone, inside a rim, and most are full of blown sand. A few near villages are clean, with a white crust on the floor.
codex.read:site:pan: Sea water left in a cut like this dries in the sun to salt, with no fuel spent. Every charge is packed in salt. The clean pans lie near villages, where a householder still needs it.
codex.seen:site:prints: Prints in clean snow, in a short line. Nothing stands at either end, and no trail leads to the first print.
codex.read:site:prints: Elsewhere a feeder is found where nothing was, and nobody sees it come. Here the snow shows the place it came up.
codex.seen:site:quarry: Cut into the slope is a square bite with flat faces and a floor of stone. One half-dressed block stands at the foot.
codex.read:site:quarry: Ground here comes away in whole pieces, and a quarry is a squared cut. The block at the foot was being dressed and was left.
codex.seen:site:shaft: A square shaft walled in dressed stone from the turf to the floor. The walls shut out caves, water and molten rock all the way down. A chest stands at the bottom.
codex.read:site:shaft: It passes every seam of ore without a side cut and goes to the floor and nowhere else. The saw at its bottom was made for root-wood.
codex.seen:site:stump: Among whole spires of pale crystal stand others eaten down to stumps one piece high.
codex.read:site:stump: The same stumps stand wherever Sakal graze, on more than one island. Nothing else here feeds on crystal.
codex.seen:site:tree_floor: Kapok planks make a floor high among the trunks, with a lamp, a crate and a bedroll on it. Nothing leads up to it.
codex.read:site:tree_floor: Neither of the plank floors we found has steps, so they were taken up from above. The bedrolls on them work for us.
codex.seen:material:wood: Bare hands take the timber of the living ground, and it splits to planks by hand.
codex.read:material:wood: Bare hands do not break stone, and a wooden pick does. Each hardness here falls to a pick of the hardness just under it.
codex.seen:material:stone: This is the common rock under the soil. A pick brings it away as rubble, and fire closes rubble back to stone.
codex.read:material:stone: Dressed stone from the old houses needs a stone pick, where raw stone gives to a wooden one. A stone pick also takes the rock iron lies in. Stone that lies dressed long enough sets harder, it seems.
codex.seen:material:iron: Ordinary iron lies in the upper and middle rock, and a wood fire melts it to bars. It also comes out of old chests and out of the Nihirakka that nest among stored iron.
codex.read:material:iron: An iron pick lifts Hīrak whole, where a stone pick broke it to nothing. Iron is the last metal a wood fire moves.
codex.seen:material:lumenite: Rare, clear, and giving a cold light, this gem lies low in the living ground. It comes away whole under an iron pick and is cleaved on the anvil's edge. No fire moves it.
codex.read:material:lumenite: Under a Hīrak pick the black glass and the warm ore by the molten rock come away. Lees that lies uneaten sets to crystal. This is clearer, harder and deeper, and it may be lees set further still.
codex.born:material:lumenite: It is crystal that went past use. A hand drives nothing through it. Kammār calls it a stone because it takes an edge. There is a piece of it in every recall stone I cut.
codex.seen:material:cinder: Jalit ore lies in the lowest rock but one, beside the molten rock, and is still warm when cut. A furnace does not move it. It runs only in the bed of a Maruhar Furnace.
codex.read:material:cinder: Jalit cuts the Antar ore of the hollow. We take Jalit for iron that ran with the molten rock and set again all at once, close to the floor.
codex.born:material:cinder: No fire of mine moves that ore. I shape the bars you bring out of the Maruhar Furnace, and that is as far as my trade goes with it.
codex.seen:material:umbrite: Antar is the metal of the hollow's rock and is found at every height there. The bed of a Maruhar Furnace that runs Jalit runs this as well.
codex.read:material:umbrite: An Antar pick takes the Tala ore lower in the hollow. Of all the metals under the living ground, only the ore that lies on its floor is harder than Antar.
codex.born:material:umbrite: I have only ever seen it as bars peopls bring up from Under. Bring me a piece of the ore raw, if you can carry it.
codex.seen:material:noctrium: Tala is the same metal as Antar, found from the lower half of the hollow down to the standing water. The Maruhar bed leaves it as it was. A Guhamāt Furnace runs it.
codex.read:material:noctrium: Tala cuts island ore. It lies lower in the hollow than Antar, nearer the floor, and is the harder of the two.
codex.seen:material:aether: Ākās is the common metal of the islands, in more veins than iron has below. We cut it over drops that do not land. A Guhamāt Furnace runs it.
codex.read:material:aether: An Ākās pick takes the island seams that have crystal grown through them. The island metals are harder than the hollow's. Some of us read hardness as age and call the islands the oldest ground we have stood on.
codex.seen:material:prism: In these seams pale crystal has grown through the islands' metal. The crystal does not split and the metal does not bend. Only a Ratan Furnace runs it.
codex.read:material:prism: Nothing made of the living ground's own matter cuts its lowest rock. A Patik pick does. Working our own floor took both gates.
codex.seen:material:eclipse: Gahan ore lies in the lowest rock, on the floor itself, a single vein in a wide stretch. It gives a violet light. Only a Kuranga Furnace runs it.
codex.read:material:eclipse: Gahan is iron set as hard as anything sets here, lying on the floor with lees through it. Its light is the colour of the things of the dark night, and some of us say they are made of it.
codex.seen:matter:gold: Gold comes from the deep rock and stays soft. A wood fire melts it, the hammer never hardens it, and it holds no edge.
codex.read:matter:gold: Gold weights the Maruhar Lure and faces the Maruhar bowls. That kind eats stone, and gold, which gives a feeder nothing to eat, was put where the animal would lie against stone.
codex.seen:matter:lees: Feeders boiled down overnight leave a dark residue, which is packed in salt. Every householder takes it, weighed out, for anything. Feeders yield it at the kill.
codex.read:matter:lees: A sheep killed paid nothing. Lees is what is left of a feeder's body, and a sheep is no feeder.
codex.born:matter:lees: Every hearth on the road uses a pot of it a night, and most are short. Weigh it into my hand and I will carry it where it is wanted.
codex.sand:matter:lees: Lees is what the dark comes up for. We burn every kill so there is none. What a march takes from your chests goes into the fire.
codex.seen:matter:crystal: Crystal is lees set hard. Driven along cut lines it loosens what it is pointed at, and does nothing else. Shut in rock it forms geodes. In the open it stands and gives light.
codex.read:matter:crystal: The jar-shaped crystal from an old store was lees once, in a jar. Crystal is lees that nothing found. The standing crystal of the caverns is the same, set in the open where it had room to grow.
codex.born:matter:crystal: Crystal grows in dark rock, and there is no kill in it. I cut the lines to it and the arm does the rest.
codex.sand:matter:crystal: Crystal is lees gone hard. The Dāhaga take it out of the stores for the fire, with the rest.
codex.seen:matter:salt: The white crust on the floor of a clean pan breaks to nothing in the hand.
codex.read:matter:salt: Where the salt failed, a store became a nest: unsalted lees is food, and feeders came to it and bred. Every charge is packed in salt against that.
codex.seen:matter:remains: Parts as they come off a feeder: flesh, sac, dust, shard, scale. Raw, they are food to feeders. They go into baits and onto carved bone.
codex.read:matter:remains: A small feeder formed on the carved bone and stayed by the hand that carried it. It went for other feeders and left us alone. Raw remains are food. As far as we can tell, food is all it stays for.
codex.born:matter:remains: What is on the bone feeds it, and it stays for that. Raw is food to all of them. Carry it salted, or carry it well away from my pot.
codex.sand:matter:remains: Raw is food, and food draws. We burn it before dark. A peopl with a small one at its side has a bone of feeder food in its hand.
codex.seen:matter:great_remains: These are the raw remains of the strongest of a host, and they go on loosening whatever is near them. One piece goes into each furnace, bench or gate.
codex.read:matter:great_remains: Fire wakes the remains in the ring, and they loosen ore that no fire moves. A furnace like that is a store of great remains with no hand on it. It draws as a spent charge does.
codex.born:matter:great_remains: Fresh remains of the Vanahar loosen made things. An old holder's hand sets as metal sets. I want to know whether they will loosen that too.
codex.sand:matter:great_remains: Every piece you build into a furnace or a gate draws, day and night. We would burn all of it.
codex.seen:people:householders: Householders are born people who hold a house ward: a clay pot of lees and one hand on a slab of cut stone until dawn. Each has a trade for the day. Few have a house. Most walk by day from one old house to the next.
codex.read:people:householders: None of them will go to a great stone or through a gate, and they die where they are killed, with no way. That is why the hunting falls to us and the holding to them.
codex.sand:people:householders: They sit beside pots and call it holding. Their pots are what the dark comes up for, and they send peopls to the stones to fill them.
codex.seen:people:sand: These born people of the sand hold no pot and burn every kill. They live round fires on black glass. Their fighters march on the houses at dawn and turn for home at dusk.
codex.read:people:sand: A token is glass from under one of their fires, with ash through it. They burn kills hot enough to run sand to glass. Nothing would be left of a kill to boil down, or to draw.
codex.born:people:sand: They gave up the pot and burn what they kill. On their marches they break stores and burn what is in them. The Deserter sits at a pot now. He holds it badly.
codex.read:people:peopls: Each of us came up at the same place, alone and empty-handed, and long after the others. Each of us dropped the load somewhere in the road and walked on. Nobody has come up with a load or a crew.
codex.born:people:peopls: A peopl comes up at the mouth with nothing in its hands and gets up again after a killing. The ground puts you out there. You were never born anywhere.
codex.sand:people:peopls: Peopls come up out of the ground with nothing and go to the old stores. Kill one and nobody sees it go, and in the morning another is there. We see no difference between that and a host at its stones.
codex.seen:old:cutter_saw: Two-handled, steel, from the bottom of a shaft sunk to the floor. Its middle teeth are stripped and the teeth at either end are whole.
codex.read:old:cutter_saw: It goes through standing timber faster than any axe made here. It is a saw for broken root-wood, the kind crews carry at home. Someone tried it on the floor, and the floor stripped it.
codex.seen:old:ward_core: It is black, cold, and as heavy as stone many times its size. It lay under a hearthstone in an old house. No tool marks it and no fire touches it.
codex.read:old:ward_core: Set down beside the floor, it is the same black stuff. The floor is the wood cores are cut from, then. Someone here once built a hearth with a core under it, the way it is done at home.
codex.seen:old:pot_crystal: This single crystal has the form of the inside of a jar, with the clay broken off it. It came out of an old chest.
codex.read:old:pot_crystal: It breaks into ordinary crystal, enough for a staff head. A jar of lees lay where the salt failed and nothing found it, and the lees set hard, jar and all.
codex.seen:old:made_bait: It came out of an old chest, made and never laid. The remains in it are sealed in matter that lasts, and it still brings its animal up.
codex.read:old:made_bait: Two kinds of bait from two kinds of store, both made ahead and never laid, for the great stones in the order the Guide gives. Nobody came back for them.
codex.born:old:made_bait: Lay it on its altar, peopl. The forebears made it for a stone they were lost before they reached, and it works as well as one made today.
codex.sand:old:made_bait: The hunters stopped going. They walked out and burned their pots, and what they had made stayed in the stores.
codex.seen:old:old_bed: Fibre over boards, out of an old house, the same as the bedrolls we make.
codex.read:old:old_bed: Lying on it moves where a fall comes out, as with our own. The born have no way and no use for one, and one lies in every old house. Whoever lived in these houses had a way.
codex.born:old:old_bed: Those beds are no use to anyone born. The forebears had peopls working for them, as we do now, and the peopls slept on those.
codex.seen:old:recall_stone: Crystal and cut lines are set round a Hīrak gem, like a small housing. One came out of a sealed store. Desik and Rehakār sell new ones.
codex.read:old:recall_stone: Driven, it puts the bearer at the bed, awake, with nothing shed. It is warm after and will not work until it cools. It works for us and for nobody born.
codex.born:old:recall_stone: I cut new ones line for line from the old. In my hand it does nothing. It works on whatever a peopl is.
codex.seen:old:token: Sand-country fighters carry these, and the Deserter takes them. It is grey glass with ash in it. It smells of nothing.
codex.read:old:token: Spent with the Deserter, a token bought a piece a march had carried out of a store and could not burn. It charges no pot.
codex.sand:old:token: Show it at a fire and you sleep inside the light and eat. A marcher carries some in case the walk home runs past dusk.
codex.seen:ground:floor: Every shaft we dig ends at the same black face, and no pick marks it. We have taken it for a rock harder than any we know.
codex.read:ground:floor: Wood of the kind cores are cut from is black and cold and takes no mark. So is this. We think the floor is dead wood, more of it in one piece than any crew has seen.
codex.seen:ground:set: A block set in the air stays there with nothing under it. Earth, sand and stone all stay as they are put.
codex.read:ground:set: Cut a tree at the foot and the rest hangs in the air. At home ground holds that steady only over a ward core. Here it holds everywhere we have cut.
codex.seen:ground:way: One of us beaten to the end of strength goes from the ground and comes to at the last bed lain on, hurt, hungry and short of lees. A bed in the hollow or on the islands marks nothing.
codex.read:ground:way: A recall stone does on purpose what a fall does, without the shedding. So the way each of us came up by is still open behind us, and a body that lets go drops into it.
codex.born:ground:way: A peopl who goes down gets up at its bed, so lie down where you want to get up. We look for you back by morning.
codex.sand:ground:way: Kill a peopl and nobody sees it go. In the morning it is back at the stores. That is why we class you with what a store draws.
codex.seen:ground:light: Nothing comes up where a torch or a lamp throws its light. In the dark, at night or under rock, feeders are found where nothing was.
codex.read:ground:light: A Tama came up in the dark and walked into the torchlight. Light stops them coming up in a place and does nothing to one already up.
codex.seen:ground:moon: The moon rises as the sun sets and sets as it rises. A round dark lies across its face and moves from night to night.
codex.read:ground:moon: On the night the moon was wholly dark, Chandasāvak came up everywhere and the sky took their colour. At dawn the sun took apart every one still standing. Even moonlight may be enough to keep them under.
codex.born:ground:moon: On the dark night the moon is hollow, and what was in it can come down. I tell every peopl which night it falls. That night, be inside walls with a lamp, or out where you mean to fight.
codex.seen:ground:ward: A householder keeps one hand on a slab of cut stone all night, with a pot of lees beside it and no core. While the hand is there, nothing comes up near the house.
codex.read:ground:ward: At dusk the packs walked in past the held room. A charge turns only what is weaker than the kill in it, and two held hearths draw. A pack led by something stronger crosses.
codex.born:ground:ward: A pot and a hand, peopl. That is a hearth. I sit at it from dusk to first light. Your own bed is no hearth, because nobody holds at it.
codex.sand:ground:ward: A pot is a store, and stores draw. A hand on it draws more. A house with a pot in it is what the dark comes up for.
codex.seen:ground:hosts: Since the first great kill, everything that comes up hits harder and takes more killing. At dusk, packs go for the houses.
codex.read:ground:hosts: It happened again with the second kind. Among feeders a kill is eaten and the eater followed. We boil ours down, and nothing is followed. The host breaks into packs that feed and grow.
codex.born:ground:hosts: Each great one was set over its country by the forebears when they raised the stones. Kill it and that country is taken back. Kill them all and the stones can be lit again.
codex.sand:ground:hosts: A great one that nothing hunts holds its country. Ours let nothing else come up on the sand. Kill one and its kind run loose, and they go where things are stored.
codex.seen:ground:mouth: Each of us came up on this same low, dry, open ground, alone and with nothing. A fall with no bed laid ends here as well. Nothing is built on it.
codex.read:ground:mouth: Dug down, it is the same floor as anywhere, with no hole in it. The road we came by meets the floor here. Only a pathfinder could step back down into it, and none of us is one.
codex.born:ground:mouth: That is where the ground puts out peopls, with nothing in their hands. None of us sleeps on it or digs there.
